source: Gyurme Dorje (2001), translated White Beryl ch.27 thirteen Bal-mo lding-skor charts; conclusion Moonbeams f39a–40a

anchor.primary_witness: White Beryl ff.314b–322a and Moonbeams conclusion ff39a–40a, via 2001 English edition

source_notes.paraphrase: The simplified thirteen Bal-mo lding-skor charts derive from a more elaborate method said to use 2,920 pebbles, and an intermediate abridged 872-pebble method (371 basic and 501 symbolic). The simplified charts have five calculations each, not eight.

anchor.primary_witness: White Beryl ff.314b–322a and Moonbeams conclusion ff39a–40a, via 2001 English edition

source_notes.paraphrase: Each of thirteen Bal-mo charts compares the selected basis with five personal axes: vitality, body, destiny, luck and numeric square. Five positions per chart give 65 simplified basic comparisons across all thirteen.

anchor.primary_witness: White Beryl ff.314b–322a and Moonbeams conclusion ff39a–40a, via 2001 English edition

source_notes.paraphrase: In Bal-mo, mother/friend and Earth/Water identity produce white; son/enemy and Wood/Iron/Fire identity produce black. In contrast the thirty computational charts encode son as one white and one black marker; color rules cannot be shared without a method flag.

anchor.primary_witness: White Beryl ff.314b–322a and Moonbeams conclusion ff39a–40a, via 2001 English edition

source_notes.paraphrase: The author describes enemy relations as especially adverse within the thirteen-chart scheme. This is a textual prioritization of symbolism, not an empirically demonstrated risk threshold.

anchor.primary_witness: White Beryl ff.314b–322a and Moonbeams conclusion ff39a–40a, via 2001 English edition

source_notes.paraphrase: Chart one White Garuda begins by counting backwards from the bird year whose element is enemy-related to the subject's constitution, and assigns five claims about royal residence, government, and status.

anchor.primary_witness: White Beryl ff.314b–322a and Moonbeams conclusion ff39a–40a, via 2001 English edition

source_notes.paraphrase: Chart two White Snowlion begins backwards from a Hare-year enemy relation for a spiritual friend; its five claims concern a throne, offerings, religious commitments and attributed blessings.

anchor.primary_witness: White Beryl ff.314b–322a and Moonbeams conclusion ff39a–40a, via 2001 English edition

source_notes.paraphrase: The Gold Snake chart three counts backwards from a Snake year in friend relation for mantrins. The Turquoise Dragon chart four counts backwards from a Dragon year in mother relation for Bon priests, giving different input/predicate paths.

anchor.primary_witness: White Beryl ff.314b–322a and Moonbeams conclusion ff39a–40a, via 2001 English edition

source_notes.paraphrase: Steadfast Elephant chart five targets ministers, Striped Tiger chart six adult males and Red Owl chart seven women/nuns, with differing starting animal year and elemental relation rather than only changing the chart title.

anchor.primary_witness: White Beryl ff.314b–322a and Moonbeams conclusion ff39a–40a, via 2001 English edition

source_notes.paraphrase: Fiery Gemstone chart eight concerns children and Blue Peacock chart nine young wives. The source assigns vitality/body/destiny/luck/mewa outcome claims to these roles; they are not generic individual horoscope traits.

anchor.primary_witness: White Beryl ff.314b–322a and Moonbeams conclusion ff39a–40a, via 2001 English edition

source_notes.paraphrase: Chart ten Gold Tiger/Dragon/Turtle/Bird concerns servants, chart eleven Golden Estate land and treasure, and chart twelve Golden Vase valuables/metals, with distinct source starting years and target outcomes.

anchor.primary_witness: White Beryl ff.314b–322a and Moonbeams conclusion ff39a–40a, via 2001 English edition

source_notes.paraphrase: Chart thirteen Adult Wild Yak concerns horses, sheep and cattle; source gives a worked start from Fire Ox for Wood-element subject but omits clear backward/forward wording in the quoted English passage. Preserve direction as unknown pending the original table.

anchor.primary_witness: White Beryl ff.314b–322a and Moonbeams conclusion ff39a–40a, via 2001 English edition

source_notes.paraphrase: In conclusion, the translator states that practical implementation of the painted computations without living oral transmission is extraordinarily difficult, while the source's divinatory status is discussed within Buddhist relative-truth doctrine. This is a source-access limit, not evidence of predictive success.

anchor.primary_witness: White Beryl ff.314b–322a and Moonbeams conclusion ff39a–40a, via 2001 English edition

source_notes.paraphrase: The conclusion quotes Moonbeams as intentionally leaving destructive/hostile divination methods to more detailed works, alongside a devotional closing. This restricts coverage: absence in the supplied book is not proof the larger tradition lacks those methods.

bounded_coverage: All thirteen simplified charts at method/role level plus author/editor conclusion; no claim of full original Tibetan direct translation.
source_ambiguities: Five-pebble Bal-mo color semantics cannot reuse eight-pebble 30-chart son-relation mixed color.
Thirteen chart 13 example states 'counting from Fire Ox' without a direction in the English excerpt; do not invent.
The work itself says the practical algorithms require oral knowledge and rare commentary beyond the book.
The alternative 2920 count also arises elsewhere in a different large public funerary ceremony; counts do not make methods identical.
next_research_frontier: After PDF400 conclusion, finish Cornu, Henning, Erlewine, Janson and directly inspect original Tibetan witnesses for source conflicts; no further core Dorje exposition until note/bibliography checks.
